blocks.text: James Skinner, General Manager, Evans-Lee
Dear Mr. Skinner:

This letter sets the terms on which this office will perform the Roadway Widening Study for {{fact:f:E-2005-001.client}}. It is a fixed-fee study with a defined scope and a set schedule. Read it. If it states the work correctly, sign both copies and return one to this office. On receipt it becomes our agreement, and we will proceed.
Scope of the Study

We will study the widening of the roadway that serves the Evans-Lee site and report what the widening requires. The study covers the existing roadway and its right-of-way, the traffic the widened section must carry, the geometry of the widened section, the drainage the widening affects, and the utilities in its path. We will identify the conflicts, size the improvements in concept, and set out what each option costs. We will not prepare construction drawings under this agreement. Construction drawings follow the study, under a separate agreement, if you elect to build.
How We Will Proceed

We begin with the existing conditions. We compile the survey, the right-of-way records, and the utility records, and we walk the roadway to confirm what the records show. From that base we set the design controls: the design speed, the lane and shoulder widths, and the sight distance the widened section must meet. We then develop the widening options that fit those controls, test each against the drainage and the utilities, and carry the workable options to a concept-level cost. The study closes with a written report and a recommendation.
Information We Rely On

Our study rests on the survey, the right-of-way records, and the utility records furnished to us or drawn from the public record. We will check that information for internal consistency, but we are entitled to rely on it, and we are not responsible for errors it carries. If the site plan or the record information changes after we begin, the change may move the findings, the schedule, and the fee. We will tell you the effect before we act on it.
The Report

The study delivers a written report. The report states the existing conditions, the design controls, the widening options we tested, and the recommendation among them, and it carries a concept-level opinion of probable construction cost for the recommended option. The report is prepared for your use in deciding whether and how to advance to design. It is a study, not a construction document, and it does not authorize construction.
The Team

Linda George, Project Engineer, will lead the study and set the roadway geometry and the grading. Jeffrey Perez, Design Technician, will prepare the base sheets and the exhibits and check the utility records against the corridor. I will review the work and seal the report. Direct the day-to-day questions to Linda George. Direct questions on scope, fee, or these terms to me.
Fee and Commencement

Our fee for the study is a fixed sum of {{fact:f:E-2005-001.fee}}. The fee covers the work described above, the report, and the recommendation. We will begin on {{fact:f:E-2005-001.start}}. The study runs about four months from that point, provided the survey and the record information reach us when the work needs them. Work outside this scope, including construction drawings, options beyond those we agree to study, or attendance at public hearings, proceeds only on your written authorization, and we will quote its cost before we take it up.
Billing and Payment

We invoice monthly, for the share of the work completed in the month. Each invoice is due within thirty days of its date. Reimbursable expenses, including reproduction, record fees, and delivery, are billed at cost and are additional to the fee. If an invoice stands unpaid for sixty days, we may suspend the work until it is paid. We will give you written notice before we suspend, and a suspension extends the schedule by its own length.
Term and Termination

This agreement takes effect on the day the work begins and runs until we deliver the report and the recommendation. Either party may end it on ten days' written notice. If you end it, you pay for the work performed and the expenses incurred through the date it ends. The report, the exhibits, and the files we prepare are our instruments of service and remain ours. On payment in full, you may use them for this project.
Confidential Information

We will hold the site information, the development plans, and the figures you give us in confidence, and we will use them only for this study. We may disclose what a public agency requires for its review of the work and what the law compels. This obligation outlasts the study.
Limit of Liability

We will perform this study with the care and skill that civil engineers in this locality ordinarily use at this time. We give no other warranty, express or implied. Our total liability to {{fact:f:E-2005-001.client}} for any claim arising out of this work, whether in contract or in tort, is limited to the fee paid under this agreement. We are not responsible for the means or the safety of any construction that may follow, nor for the acts of contractors or others not under our direct control.
Governing Law
The laws of the state in which the roadway lies govern this agreement. A dispute under it that we cannot settle between us goes to the courts of that state.
To Proceed

If these terms are correct, sign both copies where indicated and return one to this office. We will then schedule the study to begin on the date stated above. If any term needs discussion, telephone me and we will settle it before the work starts.
Sincerely,
To: The study team
From: Jeffrey Perez, Design Technician
Re: Kickoff, Roadway Widening Study for Evans-Lee

We are starting the roadway widening study for {{fact:f:E-2005-001.client}}. The aim is a clear report that says what the widening of the corridor requires and what it will cost, backed by work the client can rely on. This memo sets out who carries what and where we begin.

The deliverable is a written report with a recommendation and a concept-level opinion of cost. It is a study, not a construction set. Nothing we draw here goes out under seal until the study is finished and the report is reviewed.

We begin the study on {{fact:f:E-2005-001.start}}. James Skinner, the General Manager at Evans-Lee, is the client's contact. Route anything we need from the owner through Linda George, so the firm speaks to the client with one voice.

The study runs about four months. That is workable for a corridor of this size if we keep the base clean and settle it before we test options on it. We lose the time by drawing options on a base that later has to move.
Who carries what

The work divides the way we usually split a study of this size. Linda George leads it and owns the roadway geometry, the grading, and the coordination with the client. I build the base sheets and the exhibits and keep the utility and drainage information current on them.

items: Existing conditions and base sheets: Jeffrey Perez. I compile the survey, the right-of-way records, and the utility records, and set the base sheet the study is drawn on.
Roadway geometry and grading: Linda George. Linda sets the design controls and the widening options and carries the client coordination.
Drainage and utility checks: shared. Linda sets the approach; I test each option against the drainage and the utilities in the corridor and flag the conflicts.
Cost opinion and report: Linda George, with my exhibits. Linda writes the recommendation; I prepare the figures and the report exhibits.

blocks.text: The record comes first

A widening study is only as good as the record it rests on. So the first effort goes to the survey, the right-of-way, and the utility records, and we will not test an option until that base is confirmed. Check every callout against the design memoranda, not against memory.

Everything gets logged to the project folder as it comes in. The survey, the record prints, and the utility information go to the lettered folder, and each base sheet references the memorandum that governs it. Keep the folder current, so the exhibits at the end are built on filed information and not on loose prints.
First steps

Linda George will confirm the design controls and the corridor limits with the client. I will pull the survey and the records and stand up the base sheet. Once the base is confirmed, we lay out the widening options and begin the drainage and utility checks.
The first step is mine. I will have the base sheet and the record set assembled for Linda George to review by the end of the week.
Working Session Minutes

Project: Roadway Widening Study for {{fact:f:E-2005-001.client}}. Subject: working session on the existing conditions and the widening options for the corridor. Prepared by Linda George, Project Engineer.
Attendees
Discussion

The session confirmed that the study has moved past the compilation of the record and onto the corridor itself, and it settled three matters: that the existing-conditions base is sound enough to build the options on, that two utility conflicts along the corridor will govern which of the widening options remain workable, and that the owner will supply the traffic counts and the current site plan on which the geometry and the corridor limits depend.

Linda George opened by walking the meeting through the existing-conditions base as it now stands, describing the survey coverage of the roadway and its right-of-way, the record information gathered on the utilities in the corridor, and the field observations taken to confirm what the records show, and it was agreed that the base has reached the stage at which the widening options can be laid out on it without the risk that a later correction to the base would undo the work already done.

Jeffrey Perez reported on the utility and drainage information he has posted to the base sheets, noting in particular two points at which an existing utility sits within the width the widened roadway would have to take, and it was discussed that these two conflicts are the constraints most likely to decide among the widening options, so that each option carried forward will be tested against them before it is developed in any further detail.

James Skinner set out what the owner needs from the study, which is a clear account of what the widening requires and of what it will cost, and he agreed to furnish the traffic counts and the current site plan for the development, both of which the geometry and the corridor limits depend upon, and it was understood on all sides that the options cannot be fixed until those two items are in hand.

On the schedule it was noted that the study stands in its early phase, with the existing conditions established and the options not yet compared, and that the pace from this point will be set by how quickly the traffic counts and the site plan are returned, since the geometry cannot be fixed nor the cost opinion begun until the corridor limits are settled against the owner's current plan for the site.
Action Items

rows: Lay out the widening options on the confirmed existing-conditions base
Test each option against the two utility conflicts in the corridor
Furnish the traffic counts and the current site plan
Confirm the corridor limits once the site plan is in hand
On receipt of the site plan

blocks.text: The next working session will be scheduled once the widening options are laid out and the traffic counts are in hand, so that the session can be spent on comparing the options rather than on establishing the base a second time.
Roadway Widening Study: Progress Report

The Roadway Widening Study for {{fact:f:E-2005-001.client}} is at its midpoint and on schedule. The existing conditions are established, the widening options are laid out on them, and the work has moved to comparing the options. The study remains within the fixed fee of {{fact:f:E-2005-001.fee}}.

This report is prepared for Evans-Lee. It covers the current period, and it states what was finished, what comes next, and the items that could affect the schedule. It is written for the client and is deliberately short.

The period since the last report went to two things: finishing the existing-conditions base and laying the widening options onto it. Both are done. The study now turns to comparing the options, which is the work of the coming weeks.
Where the Study Stands
The study is about half complete and tracking to the plan. The existing-conditions base is set, and the widening options rest on it. No change to the scope or the fee is anticipated.

The work is proceeding in the order the design requires: from the records to the base, from the base to the options, and next from the options to the cost. Linda George leads the study and has fixed the design controls for the widened section. The comparison now under way is the same kind of work as the base already finished, so nothing ahead of us on this corridor is unfamiliar.
Work Completed This Period

The existing-conditions base was finished and checked. The survey coverage of the roadway and its right-of-way, the record information on the utilities in the corridor, and the field observations taken to confirm the records were compiled onto the base sheets. The roadway was walked so the base rests on what is there and not on the record alone.

The widening options were laid out on that base. Linda George set the design controls, the lane and shoulder widths, and the sight-distance requirements the widened section must meet, and the options were framed to those controls. Each option follows a workable line through the corridor rather than a single assumed section.

The utility and drainage information was posted to the base. Two conflicts were identified in the corridor, at points where an existing utility sits within the width the widened roadway would take. Each option carried forward is being tested against those two conflicts.

The project folder was brought current for the period. The survey, the record prints, and the utility information are filed, and each base sheet references the memorandum that governs it, so the exhibits built later rest on filed information.
Work Ahead

The next period compares the options against the design controls, the two utility conflicts, and the drainage, and narrows them to the ones worth costing. We will then prepare a concept-level opinion of probable construction cost for each option that survives the comparison.

The corridor limits still depend on the current site plan and the traffic counts for the development. The comparison can proceed on the base as it stands, but the options cannot be fixed, nor the cost opinion closed, until those two items are in hand and the limits are confirmed against them.
From the costed options, Linda George will settle a recommendation, and I will assemble the report exhibits that support it. The study closes with the written report and that recommendation.
Budget

The study remains within the fixed fee of {{fact:f:E-2005-001.fee}}. The effort spent to date is in line with the portion of the work that is complete. No additional services have been requested, and none are foreseen under the current scope.
Items to Watch

items: Traffic counts and site plan: the geometry and the corridor limits depend on the counts and the current site plan; the options cannot be fixed until both are in hand.
Utility conflicts: the two conflicts in the corridor may narrow the workable options and will be confirmed against the record before any option is costed.
Client review turnaround: the schedule assumes the study's questions to the owner are answered promptly.
Site access: any field check of a grade or a utility depends on access to the corridor.

blocks.text: The next step is to finish comparing the widening options and bring the workable ones to a concept-level cost. We will send the results to Evans-Lee as soon as that comparison is complete. Prepared by Jeffrey Perez, Design Technician.
